planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; this all-green sport of 'Manjula' tolerates dimmer rooms better than its variegated parent.

directions: Grow as a houseplant in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix. Because this sport of 'Manjula' lacks the white and cream sectoring of its parent, it carries more chlorophyll and tolerates dimmer rooms without stretching or losing color. Leaves are broad and gently ruffled at the edge in a solid medium green with only faint pale flecking near the petiole. It climbs or trails vigorously once established and roots readily from single-node cuttings in water or moist mix.

planting.note: Train onto a moss pole or bark slab in bright indirect light so the plant reaches the mature, lance-shaped leaf form that shows off this cultivar's cream-and-white marbling.

directions: Train onto a moss pole or bark slab in bright indirect light so the plant can reach the mature, lance-shaped leaf form that shows this cultivar's cream-and-white marbling along the silvery midrib stripe; juvenile trailing growth stays smaller, heart-shaped, and less consistently variegated. Because the white sectors carry no chlorophyll, this form grows more slowly than the plain green species and needs brighter light to avoid reverting toward solid green. Keep the growing medium evenly moist but well drained in warm, humid conditions typical of a tropical aroid collection. Propagate from stem cuttings that include at least one node of solid green tissue to preserve vigor.

planting.note: Provide a moss pole or trellis in bright indirect light to bring out the gold-and-green mottled foliage; unsupported trailing growth stays smaller and more solid-colored.

directions: Provide a moss pole or trellis in bright indirect light to bring out this cultivar's bold gold-and-green mottled foliage, which holds its warm coloring better with more light than a shaded trailing position allows. Leaves follow the same lance-shaped, eventually fenestrating growth habit as other pinnatum selections, with variegation that runs buttery yellow rather than silvery blue-green. Young, unsupported growth stays smaller and more solid-colored, with the strongest gold patterning appearing once the vine is trained upward and matures. Root single-node stem cuttings in water or moist mix to propagate.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light in a chunky, well-drained mix; let the mix dry between waterings since the fleshy leaves store water and rot easily if kept wet.

directions: Grow as a houseplant in bright, indirect light in a well-drained, chunky potting mix; this Costa Rican species forms a dense rosette of thick, glossy, deeply quilted dark green leaves with a slightly succulent texture. It stays compact and slow-growing compared with trailing peperomias, making it well suited to a windowsill or tabletop rather than a hanging basket. Let the top of the potting mix dry between waterings, since the fleshy leaves and stems store water and are prone to rot if kept constantly moist. Propagate from leaf or stem cuttings rooted in a light, well-aerated mix.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; tolerates dim interior corners as well as other deremensis-type dracaenas.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix. 'Rikki' produces narrower, more lax leaves than Janet Craig, in solid deep green with a glossy sheen, arching outward from a slow-forming cane rather than standing stiffly upright. It tolerates the same dim interior corners and irregular watering that make dracaenas popular office and lobby plants, and rarely needs repotting more than once every few years. Water only once the top half of the potting mix has dried, and avoid cold drafts below about 55F.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; needs more light than solid-green dracaenas to keep its white striping from fading.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; 'White Jewel' needs a bit more light than solid green dracaenas to keep its broad white-and-light-green central striping from fading toward plain green. Leaves are glossy, strap-shaped, and wider than many deremensis-type cultivars, arching from a slow-growing cane. It shares the group's tolerance for missed waterings and indoor conditions, but the variegated tissue scorches more easily in direct sun than the solid green forms. Let the top half of the potting mix dry before watering again.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; tolerates dim corners as well as Warneckii.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix. 'Malaika' carries broad, irregular stripes of gray-green, white, and creamy yellow-green down each strap-shaped leaf, giving a softer, more pastel look than the stronger white-on-green contrast of Warneckii. It grows at the same unhurried pace as other dracaena cultivars and tolerates the dim corners and inconsistent watering typical of indoor settings. Water once the top half of the potting mix has dried and keep it away from cold drafts below 55F.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; tolerates dim interior light as well as Janet Craig.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix. 'Hawaiian Sunshine' produces glossy, deep green leaves brightened by a crisp light-green center stripe running the length of each blade, giving a cleaner, higher-contrast look than plain Janet Craig. It forms an upright cane over time and shares the group's easy tolerance of dim interior light and irregular watering. Water only once the top half of the potting mix has dried out, and protect it from temperatures below 55F.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; the chartreuse new growth holds its color best with a bit more light than plain Janet Craig needs.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; the twisting, slightly curled leaves emerge chartreuse-yellow before settling into a gray-green center flanked by darker green margins, a more vividly colored and texturally distinct form than most straight-leaved dracaena cultivars. It keeps the group's compact, slow-growing cane habit and general tolerance for indoor conditions, but the brighter leaf color holds best with a bit more light than Janet Craig needs. Water once the top half of the potting mix has dried, and keep it away from cold drafts below 55F.
